archetype.name: Playoff Team (short-handed contender)
archetype.definition: A roster that won 68 and 64 games in the last two seasons, now playing at a playoff team's level rather than a champion's because most of its top talent is listed out, with an elite defense carrying an ordinary offense.

report.headline: A champion's defense holding the line while the stars sit in street clothes
report.take:
Look at the injury column before the record. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is listed out, and so are Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Aday Mara and Jaylin Williams. Jalen Williams and Holmgren have three games each. This is the team that went 68-14 and won the title two seasons ago, then went 64-18 last year with the league's top defense both times. At 10-7, fourth in a crowded Northwest, and 16th on the site, it is not playing like that team. It is playing like a solid playoff team, and the margin backs up the record: W vs Pt Diff is exactly 0, and the differential implies 10 wins, the number it has.

The defense is still championship-grade. A 110.5 DRtg ranks 5th, and opponents are shooting 56.7% at the rim, the best mark in the league and 8.6 points under the league average. That is a frontcourt identity, not a one-man one. Isaiah Hartenstein sits 10th on the center tab with 181 rebounds, and the frontcourt grades B+ even with Holmgren and Mara listed out. The ball security is also intact: a 11.7 TOV % ranks 3rd, right in line with the franchise's recent seasons.

The offense is where the absences show. ORtg is 114.2, 15th and almost exactly league average, after 118.9 last season. The shot profile has changed with it. A 35.4 3PA Rate ranks 29th, down from 42.6 a year ago, and a 24.1 FT Rate ranks 27th. Without its creators, this offense isn't generating threes or free throws, and TS % has fallen to 56.3, 23rd. Gilgeous-Alexander's numbers show how much leans on him: a 36.9 USG %, a 7.9 BPM and a +10 On-Off. Jared McCain has taken on big minutes at a 53.7 TS % with a -10 On-Off, and that is the hole the missing stars leave.

The month-to-month line hides some real movement. October's offense scored 106.5 a game, November's 116.55, so the scoring has come around. But the last five games allowed 115.2 a game, nearly six points worse than the season, and they produced a 2-3 stretch that included two losses at Portland and a one-point loss at the Clippers. The direction from here depends almost entirely on who comes back and when. A healthy version of this roster has two seasons of evidence behind it. The current one is a top-10 team by margin playing on defense alone.

strengths.title: Best rim protection in the league
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 56.7% at the rim, first in the league and far below the league mean. They also get there less often than average, with a 27.1 Opp Rim Rate that ranks 7th. That holds with Holmgren and Mara out, which points to Hartenstein and team structure rather than one shot-blocker. Interior defense this strong across two straight top-ranked defensive seasons looks durable.

strengths.title: Hartenstein anchors a B+ frontcourt
strengths.body: The frontcourt carries the best grade on the roster. Hartenstein, 10th of 92 on the center tab, has played every game and leads the team in rebounds by a wide margin. That keeps REB % above water at 9th even with two big men listed out. He is the reason the defense hasn't collapsed without its stars.

strengths.title: Possessions rarely wasted
strengths.body: An 11.7 TOV % ranks 3rd, a franchise trait that has held through every recent season. With an offense that doesn't get to the line or launch threes, not giving away possessions is what keeps it at league average instead of below it.

concerns.title: Offense shrank without its creators
concerns.body: ORtg sits 15th at 114.2, down from 118.9 last season. The shot diet explains it: the 3PA Rate has fallen to 29th and the FT Rate to 27th. Those are the shots a primary creator generates, and Gilgeous-Alexander carries a 36.9 USG % and is listed out. This should ease as players return, but until then the offense has no engine.

concerns.title: Defense has leaked lately
concerns.body: Over the last five games OKC allowed 115.2 a game, well above its season rate, and went 2-3. Losses to Portland twice, Atlanta and Miami came against opponents who scored freely. It is a small sample against a strong season baseline, but it is the first crack in the one unit propping everything up.

concerns.title: Backcourt minutes going to a weak link
concerns.body: McCain has the second-most minutes on the team but posts a -2.5 BPM and a -10 On-Off on 53.7 TS %. Bennett Stirtz, meanwhile, is shooting 65.8 TS % in a smaller role. With the star guard out, how those minutes get split matters more than usual.

trend.note: The scoring jumped from 106.5 a game in October to 116.55 in November, but the last ten split 5-5. Blowouts of Memphis and Washington sat next to close losses, and the defense slipped over the final five.

weekAhead.headline: Three bottom-tier opponents and Minnesota, with Gilgeous-Alexander listed out
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games come against teams ranked 23rd or worse on the site. Indiana is 5-12, Milwaukee 1-16 and Brooklyn 3-12. Milwaukee and Brooklyn bring defenses ranked 30th and 26th, which is exactly the kind of opponent a sputtering half-court offense can score on. Three of the four are on the road, but this is a schedule that should cover for a thin roster and could reverse the recent slide.

The exception is Minnesota at home. The Timberwolves are 12-5, second on the site and first in the division, with the league's best DRtg at 104.5 and the best Opp eFG %. Against that defense, an offense that doesn't take threes or draw fouls will struggle to find points. Three wins out of the soft games would be par, and a split with Minnesota would be a bonus.

keyMatchups.title: Minnesota's top-ranked defense
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota allows a 104.5 DRtg, first in the league, and leads in Opp eFG %. This is the hardest test available for an offense ranked 15th that lives inside the arc. It doubles as a division game against the team OKC trails.

keyMatchups.title: Hartenstein against Milwaukee's F frontcourt
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee carries the league's worst DRtg and an F frontcourt grade. Its centers' points, rebounds and assists run further above their own averages than against any other team. That sets up as Hartenstein's best night of the week and a chance for OKC to win inside.

keyMatchups.title: Brooklyn's soft rim, stingy on PGs
keyMatchups.body: Brooklyn ranks 24th in Opp Rim FG %, so the paint should be open. Its defense has held point guards furthest below their averages in the league, though, so the scoring needs to come from the bigs and wings, not the point guards. Indiana's league-worst ORB % also hands OKC's rebounders an edge earlier in the week.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the defense returns to its season level against weak offenses after leaking points over the last five games.

restOfSeason.body:
The record is honest: the margin implies exactly the 10 wins OKC has, so expect no luck correction in either direction. What will move is the roster. At its current level, a top-10 Net Rtg and a top-five defense, this pace lands in the high 40s. That is a playoff seed in a Northwest where Minnesota, Denver and Portland are all bunched ahead. The defensive foundation looks sustainable, given the rim protection and two straight seasons ranked first.

The upside comes from the offense, which should recover sharply once Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams and Holmgren are back. The last two seasons ran at ORtgs of 120.3 and 118.9 with this core. With 65 games left, even a partial return of that version pushes this team well past its current pace. Prolonged absences keep it a mid-pack playoff team. I project 47 to 55 wins, with the Net Rtg climbing as the roster fills in.
swingFactors: Jalen Williams and Holmgren getting healthy together
Whether the rim defense survives the frontcourt injuries

confidence.note: 17 games, and the injury list makes the current roster unlike the one that will finish.
